mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months raises the cost of capital, depressing corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25pp per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls YoY for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive or flat in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with lower earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 2% for three months signals a monetary policy tightening in the face of rising prices, which historically has been associated with higher discount rates and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed thresholds concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average, coupled with a concurrent fall in personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing demand shock that reduces construction and retail activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 6-month MA AND RSAFS < 6-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 35% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE ≤ 5%), signals a strong demand-driven expansion that boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA for 6 consecutive months AND UNRATE ≤ 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 50% of co-triggered episodes.
